# P32.16a — Apply approved corrections through the canonical disposition path

**Requirement ids:** SIG-FIND-008 (§55) ·
**ADR:** none new — executes ADR-135's stated follow-up through the already-decided canonical machinery (§16.6, ADR-124) ·
**Base:** `devin/p32-16-anonymous-correction-intake` (stacked on PR #172 — merge this after #172) ·
**Run:** `implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/177_P32.16a__reviewed-correction-application.md live_verification=false` ·
**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/177_P32.16a__reviewed-correction-application.md` (manifest row 177)

## What this does

Delivers the **reviewed-correction application bridge** — SIG-FIND-008. The
durable anonymous receiver shipped by P32.16 (ADR-135) deliberately stopped
short of the canonical graph: `applied`/`published` were refused under every
role, and the writer guard named P32.16a as their owner. This PR is that
bridge. An **approved** proposal — and only an approved one — can now apply
through the canonical correction/disposition writes in one transaction, with
an append-only receipt, an `op-` operation id for exactly-once
reconciliation, and a separate publish-linkage step. There is **no parallel
write path**: every refusal returns before a canonical mutation, the reporter
is never `asserted_by`, and `refuse` never reaches the bridge. **Nothing here
applies a correction in production** — `D-P32.16-1` and `D-R10-PUBLISH-1`
stay OPEN by design.

### The bridge role — `sig_intake_bridge` (`db/deploy/intake_application_bridge.sql`)

- Third NOLOGIN least-privilege intake role; the ONLY role the
  `current_setting('role')` writer guard now admits `applied`/`published`
  under (receiver/reviewer refusals are proven in the grants-matrix tests).
- Column-scoped canonical grants only: `INSERT claim`, `UPDATE (sys_period)
  claim` (close the prior belief — the single permitted claim mutation,
  ADR-124), `claim_evidence`, the guarded entity mint (`entity`,
  `entity_identifier`, `entity_identity_key`), `ingest_run`,
  `INSERT/SELECT publication_disposition` + sequence. No review_decision,
  capture, extraction or payload writes; no UPDATE anywhere else.
- `sig_read_sealed` membership — read-scope only — so the apply can read the
  target claim at whatever tier the report cited (claim is FORCE-RLS) and
  re-check that tier before writing.
- New append-only `intake.application` receipt: immutable
  `application_id`/`receipt`/`from_payload`/`ref`/`evidence_sha` (CHECK),
  `UNIQUE(operation_id)`, `application_id` ↔ claim/disposition links,
  publish-linkage columns (`publication_id`, `correction_ref`, `tombstone`).
- `disposition_approved → disposition_proposed` transition added (with the
  reciprocal re-approval already present): a stale/refused apply is
  superseded by a re-proposal + re-approval rather than dead-ending the
  report; the writer guard still requires the approval to be the LATEST
  lifecycle event at apply time.

### The bridge — `db/src/db/intake_apply.py`

- `pg_advisory_xact_lock` keyed on the receipt serializes apply AND publish
  linkage per report — deliberately not `FOR UPDATE`: the bridge holds no
  UPDATE grant on the immutable `intake.report`, and row locks would not
  cover `mark_published` anyway.
- Exactly-once: if the latest event is `applied`, the committed application
  row is returned verbatim (`reconciled: true`) — this is also the
  retry-after-commit path, since the row and the `applied` event are written
  in one transaction. Otherwise the latest event must be
  `disposition_approved` naming a same-outcome proposal via `approves_seq`;
  the deterministic `op-<uuid5(report, approval_seq, outcome)>` (or a caller
  `operation_id`) is then reconciled by id — same-op row = retry,
  different-op row = `conflict`, absent = apply; a `UniqueViolation` races
  to the same lookup. A re-approved proposal derives a NEW approval seq → a
  NEW operation id → applies fresh.
- Re-validate everything at apply time — `policy.intake.validate_proposal`
  (same validator the moderation route runs at write), claim open +
  `ref`-pinned, evidence-set digest recomputed, `correction_reason`
  allowlist, tier/rights/sensitivity re-check, Part VIII `unsafe_payload`.
- Canonical outcomes: `correct` = close the open `sys_period` + insert the
  `revises_claim` claim + `correction_reason` + rebind the same evidence
  captures — in ONE transaction; `annotate` = non-superseding claim;
  `suppress`/`delete` = append `publication_disposition` (withhold/withdraw —
  never a byte deleted); `asserted_by`/`decided_by` mint the curator's
  `sig.curator.handle` identity through `resolve_identities` (guarded,
  exact-handle scheme).

### Loopback-only routes (`api/src/api/curation.py`)

- `POST /v1/curation/intake/reports/<receipt>/apply` — tier-2 reviewer,
  proposal approval required; 201 + the applied receipt; error map keeps
  `unknown_receipt`/`expunged_report`→404,
  `no_current_approval`/`stale_record`/`record_changed`/`evidence_changed`→
  409, `permission_denied`→403, `invalid_proposal`/`unsafe_payload`/
  `conflict`/`tier_denied`/`target_denied`/`rights_denied`→4xx, and
  `503 pg_store_unavailable` when the curation store has no PG (memory
  store) — the canonical apply is DB-only by design.
- `POST /v1/curation/intake/reports/<receipt>/published` — separate from
  apply; only from `applied`; requires at least one of `publication_id`
  (`p-<64 hex>`, ADR-132), `correction_ref`, or an explicit `tombstone`;
  idempotent on a repeat identical link, 409 on a conflicting one.
- The memory store mirrors both semantics so API-level tests exercise the
  same contract; received/under_review/decided/resolved stay distinct in
  `public_state`.

### The public corrections log (`exports/src/exports/spine_export.py`, `web/`)

- `web/corrections.json` entries now name BOTH sides of a correction —
  `previous_claim_id`, `revises_claim`, `retraction_of`, `previous_value`,
  `previous_belief_date` — plus `previous_withheld: true` when the prior
  assertion exists but is not publicly eligible. The old-claim gate re-uses
  `claim_eligible_sql('oc')` — a gated prior can NEVER leak a partial value.
- `docs/build/reports/public_surface_contracts.schema.json`
  (`sig.public-corrections/1`) gains the optional linkage properties;
  `web/src/lib/corrections.ts` + `web/src/pages/corrections.astro` render an
  explicit "prior withheld" marker instead of a fabricated blank previous
  value. Zero-JS, static.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Approve→apply→restart→retry yields one canonical disposition and one
  stable applied receipt** — `UNIQUE(operation_id)` + `applied`-latest
  reconcile + `UniqueViolation`→lookup; deterministic op derivation;
  `test_apply_idempotent_reconciles`, `test_apply_concurrent`, retry-after-
  re-proposal tests.
- **Unauthorized / stale-record / changed-evidence / unsafe-payload fail
  without graph mutation** — all checks precede the canonical write inside
  one transaction; every refusal code covered by a real-PG test; `refuse`
  never reaches the bridge; moderator denial changes no facts.
- **A published correction points to old/new assertion + release identities
  or safe tombstones; received/reviewed/applied/unpublished visibly
  distinct** — publish linkage validated + idempotent; export old/new
  linkage + withheld tombstone; public-state projection unchanged.
- **Verification green; every behavior tested; deferrals owned** — below.

## Verification

`live_verification=false` — no production apply, no release published, no
hosting; all evidence offline + real-PG fixtures.

- `make check` — green: **5,172 passed / 3 skipped**, ruff + format + mypy
  (285 files) + verify-gen clean.
- `SIG_REQUIRE_DB_TESTS=1 uv run pytest tests/db` — **440 passed** on
  `postgis/postgis:18-3.6` (all 27 `test_intake_apply_pg.py`: every outcome
  and refusal, idempotent/concurrent reconcile, publish linkage +
  tombstone, grants matrix incl. receiver/reviewer write refusals,
  append-only receipt immutability, concurrent curator-entity mint,
  superseded-approval fresh re-apply).
- `sqitch deploy` + `verify` + `revert` of `intake_application_bridge` —
  green; the whole-plan revert fails at the pre-existing
  `revert/extensions.sql` postgis CASCADE defect → recorded `D-P32.16a-1`.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_intake_contract.py
  tests/api/test_curation_intake.py tests/exports/test_spine_export.py` —
  green.
- `npm --prefix web run` `typecheck` (0/141), `test:unit` (256), `build`
  (54 pages) — green.
- `scripts/docs/check-build-memory.sh .` — 0 violations.

## Deferrals

- **Opened** `D-P32.16a-1` (V) — whole-plan `sqitch revert` fails at the
  base `revert/extensions.sql` (`postgis_topology`/`postgis_tiger_geocoder`
  dependents need CASCADE); pre-existing, surfaced by this run's revert
  sweep; repair shape is a maintainer decision.
- **Annotated, stay OPEN:** `D-P32.16-1` (the bridge role is NOLOGIN with no
  login grant; staffed/reviewed curation still required) and
  `D-R10-PUBLISH-1` (machinery shipped; nothing deployed or published —
  GATE-G3 owns exposure).
- **Closed:** none.

## Out of scope (held)

Production application, any release/publication, receiver operation, gate
signatures, merges/tags/`main`. Real corrections remain a separately
authorized curator decision under the existing publication policy.
